title: The Ancient Ledger Chamber

features.name: the ledger that rewrites itself
features.desc-on-touch: Stone pages, each entry older than the last. Debts recorded in a language the bedrock speaks when nobody is watching. The sums never settle; they grow sideways instead of down.

features.name: the weight that learned to dream
features.desc-on-touch: A mass of stone compressed until it became conscious of what it owed. You feel it thinking downward, calculating an infinite debt, and knowing that being remembered is a kind of payment.

features.name: the settlement that will never come
features.desc-on-touch: An arch carved from obsidian that marks the point where debts learned they could grow. The corruption loves this place—debts multiplying without being forgiven, without being forgotten.

features.name: the roots beneath the ledger
features.desc-on-touch: Thick root systems pushing through stone, making their own entries, their own calculations. The roots owe the stone, the stone owes the roots. Neither knows how long this has been settling.

features.name: the chamber wall that counts currency
features.desc-on-touch: A surface where debts have become stone markings, calcified payment-attempts. The older debts have learned to echo newer ones. The wall hums with old arithmetic.

inscription: here the unpaid things learn that forgetting is the only possible form of payment

reverie.title: REVERIE — dusk on the red earth, the accounting
narr: you knelt beside her on the ridge where the land owed
them nothing, where they owed it everything. she traced
a line in the dust with her finger. that is what we pay
with, she said. the line. not the settling. just the mark
of trying, and the trying never finishes.
